item.description: Tamatha Paul, Green Party MP for Wellington Central in New Zealand (elected 2023). First Māori MP for that seat. She opposed it, calling English a “bastard language” (a mix of others), arguing the focus wastes time amid cost-of-living pressures, and that te reo needs protection after historical suppression. She praised Wales for prioritising Welsh.

item.title: GovBrief Today #547
item.description: A lie about paint put a 67-year-old Olympian in handcuffs. We knew nobody in Ohio was eating cats and dogs, and the vice president admitted he would "create stories" to get attention. We knew a Sharpie stretched that hurricane map into Alabama. And we knew there was no 300-foot gash in the Reflecting Pool. Trump kept lying anyway, and this time the government followed him. Park Police handcuffed Davey Hearn for touching water on a bike ride. A US Attorney announced his felony at a press conference. The truth arrived on a summer Friday afternoon, in a court filing that admits the $14.6 million paint job was "hasty and botched" and that a Park Service engineer flagged the peeling liner eight days before Hearn ever stopped his bike. The government had the answer in its inbox before it had a suspect. Governments lie to keep secrets. This lie kept a president from admitting his paint job failed. item.title: When Accountability Wears a Fucking Mask
item.description: A government that insists every civilian must instantly obey armed, masked agents has a fucking monumental obligation to ensure those agents are disciplined, accountable, and restrained. Instead, too often the response is secrecy, spin, and "trust us." ⚖️ The most dangerous phrase in any democracy isn't "national security." It's "don't ask questions." When transparency disappears behind redactions and official statements become public relations exercises, public trust dies right alongside it. Power without accountability isn't law enforcement- it's permission. And when institutions circle the wagons instead of confronting uncomfortable facts, every future tragedy becomes easier to dismiss than prevent. That's how democracies slowly rot from the inside. Nobody should have to wonder whether the full truth will ever see daylight after a government use of deadly force. Independent investigations, transparency, and accountability aren't anti-police- they're pro-democracy. Demand better. #Accountability #Transparency #CivilRights #Democracy #Justice #RuleOfLaw

item.title: The Marble City of the Sahara
item.description: Leptis Magna, on Libya’s Mediterranean coast, is widely regarded as one of the best-preserved Roman cities in the world. Founded by the Phoenicians and later transformed into a thriving Roman metropolis, the city reached its peak under Emperor Septimius Severus, who was born there. Today, visitors can still walk through remarkably intact marble streets, towering columns, temples, a grand forum, and an impressive amphitheater that have survived for nearly 2,000 years. Unlike many famous Roman archaeological sites, Leptis Magna remains largely free of crowds, with the dry desert climate helping preserve its extraordinary ruins and offering a rare glimpse into the grandeur of the Roman Empire.
